sentences.text: Kayrasaurus possessed a complete furcula, a wishbone-like bone, with a gracile V-shape typical of therizinosaurs.
The angle between the ends of this furcula was broad, measuring approximately 140 degrees.
The humerus, or upper arm bone, was unusually robust, resembling those found in Erliansaurus and Nothronychus graffami.
Unlike the bowed shaft seen in Falcarius, the shaft of the Kayrasaurus humerus was straight.
The radius, a forearm bone, was straight and slender, consistent with basal therizinosaurs.
Like other therizinosaurs, the front of the Kayrasaurus jaws were toothless.
This dinosaur was found in China.
The type locality of Kayrasaurus is the Yixian Formation.
The species was described by Liao and colleagues.
Kayrasaurus is a newly described genus and species.
Kayrasaurus is closely related to the contemporary Beipiaosaurus and Jianchangosaurus.
Most Kayrasaurus teeth were similar in size, though those closest to the front were likely larger.
Kayrasaurus neck vertebrae were pneumatized, indicated by foramina on the lateral surfaces of the centra.
The species Kayrasaurus changliensis was described by Liao et al. in 2026.
Kayrasaurus belongs to the parent group Therizinosauria.
Kayrasaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Kayrasaurus is an extinct genus of therizinosaurian dinosaur known from the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of China.
Kayrasaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
It is debated whether Kayrasaurus reached full adult size, as the specimen was likely a subadult.
